messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel selector tweak in canary (v2.3.7) I'm seeing a spike in fragmentation and a couple of KV OOMs on the 40-token fast-path. Logs attached below.
maria: saw that on prod-canary too. nvprof snapshot shows a lot more short-lived allocations in the logits scratchpad (size ~24KB) and activation staging (48KB) than before.
jamal: is this the allocator freelist compaction timing change we pushed last week? could be leaving many small slots with stale headers.
sarah: I ran a repro locally: sequence of short batched requests (batch=8, seq=40) -> allocator high watermark jumps then we hit an OOM when a 2nd micro-burst arrives.
kai: curious if KV cache interleaving is preventing reuse — when cache pages get pinned we can't evict small scratchpads, fragmentation rises.
alex: snippet from the runtime profiler (trimmed):
```
[profiler] timeline: alloc(48KB) -> free delayed 120ms -> alloc(24KB) -> alloc(48KB) -> OOM
[metrics] freelist_bins: small: 1200 free, 420 in-use, fragmentation=17%
[metrics] pool_reclaim_attempts: 3, deferred_compactions: 27
```
maria: also saw the tail-latency spikes (~150ms added) coincide with compaction events.
jamal: proposal: switch to a slot-rotation reclaim policy for small bins: instead of immediate compaction we rotate ownership of slots between streams and only compact when a bin is >75% free for >500ms.
sarah: that aligns with what we did in CPU allocator for small objects. Benefits: avoids frequent moving of live blocks during bursts. Downside: could postpone reclaim longer and raise HW watermark.
kai: alternative: credit-based reuse. Give each stream a limited credit of small slots it can hold; when credit exhausted we force-one free oldest slot. Less global compaction.
alex: both sound reasonable. Which minimizes worst-case tail latency? we want to avoid compaction pauses during steady-state batching.
jamal: credit-based probably better for latency, rotation better for fragmentation numbers. We could A/B: rotation on dedicated pools, credit on shared pools.
maria: quick config for a canary (example):
```
"pooling": {
  "small_bin_thresh": 64,         # KB
  "rotation_window_ms": 500,
  "rotation_threshold_pct": 75,
  "stream_credits": 12
}
```
sarah: also add a background low-priority compactor that runs only when overall GPU util < 60% to avoid interfering with bursts.
kai: we should also instrument per-bin age histograms so we know how long slots sit unused before reclaim — that'll validate the rotation window.
alex: ops-bot can we schedule a canary with rotation policy on canary-2 endpoint for next deploy?
ops-bot: deploy scheduled to canary-2 at 2025-04-17T21:30Z, rollout group: runtime/buffer-pools, config override: pooling.rotation_window_ms=500
maria: I'll add age histograms and per-stream credit counters to the profiler (small change). will push a patch today.
jamal: i'll implement the rotation logic and a flag to toggle credit-mode. PR target EOD.
sarah: test matrix: (1) batch=8 seq=40 microburst X, (2) batch=1 seq=2048 long-run, (3) mixed KV warmup pattern. measure fragmentation, tail-99, OOM count.
alex: action items: maria add histograms, jamal implement rotation/credit toggle, kai create canary test harness, sarah run matrix and report. ping here when canary is live.
kai: noted. I'll also add a perf regression alert for compaction-time > 50ms.
alex: thanks all — if canary looks good we'll roll to dedicated pools next week. :thumbsup:
